simple.meaning: אָכֵן (ʼâkên) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “firmly ; figuratively, surely ; also (adversative) but.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 18 times across Genesis, Exodus, 1 Samuel, 1 Kings, Job, and 4 more, beginning at Genesis 28:16. Its contexts include death, kingship, Egypt, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָכֵן (H403).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: אָכֵן (ʼâkên) / H403 is traced through Genesis 28:16, Exodus 2:14, 1 Samuel 15:32, 1 Kings 11:2 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.usage: but, certainly, nevertheless, surely, truly, verily.
definitions.full: H403. aken אָכֵן (perhaps from אַח ; compare Aramaic דֵּח & דִּכֵּן ) adverb with strong asseverative force: a. surely, truly , especially at beginning of a speech (stronger & more decided than אַח ) Gen 28:16 ; Exod 2:14 ; 1Sam 15:32 ; Isa 40:7 ; 45:15 ; Jer 3:23 (twice in verse); 4:10 ; 8:8 . In 1Kin 11:2 אָבֵן stands unusually; and מֶּןֿ (compare ᵑ7 ᵑ6 ᵐ5 ) should probably be read (so Klo). b. emphasizing a contrast , but indeed, but in fact , especially after אָמַרְתִּי I said or thought , expressing the reality, in opposed to what had been wrongly imagined, Isa 49:4 b (opposed to v a ) 53:4 (opposed to 53:3 end) Jer 3:20 (opposed to the expectation 3:19 b) Zeph 3:7 b Psa 31:23 b (opposed to 31:23 a) 66:19 ; 82:7 (opposed to 82:6 ) Job 32:8 (opposed to 32:7 ).
